transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-18
- Start: 10:30 PST
- Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
- Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Silva (Redwood CSM); Dana Morris (CTO), Jamal Reyes (Platform), Priya Kapoor (Security), Luis Ortega (SRE), Anya Levin (PM)

Summary:
Quick POC check-in focused on staging gate readiness, SSO/SAML handoff, KMS/HSM integration questions, and a short review of the first micro-benchmark runs. Agreed on next run cadence and owners for key items.

Topics:
- Staging gating checklist and who has access
- SAML/SSO integration steps and known pitfalls
- KMS key rotation and HSM routing
- Benchmark interpretation: p95/p99 tail and batching effects
- Fallback plan if Dedicated capacity hairpins

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick us off. Dana, can you confirm this is still the core POC scope? Onboarding, SSO, KMS, and the staging gate checks?
[00:18] Dana (CTO): Yes, that's right. We're mainly validating privacy controls and throughput at our expected load, which is roughly 40 to 60 concurrent sessions with short prompts. Also want SAML integrated so our folks don't need separate creds.
[00:35] Ravi (SE): Got it. Quick note — we saw the micro-benchmarks you uploaded, Jamal, thanks. There are a couple of anomalies at higher token counts where the p99 spikes, probably due to KV cache misses in those runs.
[00:50] Jamal (Platform): Yeah, some runs were on the first warm start, so cache wasn't populated. We tried a quick re-run but didn't follow exactly the warm-key pattern you recommended.
[01:05] Priya (Security): On KMS, we need clarity on where keys are stored. We use an HSM-backed KMS and require rotation every 90 days. Also SOC 2 control mapping will be required.
[01:22] Avery (AE): Perfect — we can support HSM-backed KMS. We'll share the KMS integration doc. For rotation, Redwood's private deployment supports customer-managed keys and rotation hooks. Note: sometimes our doc refers to "Redwood Private control plane" and the auto-transcript may call it "Redwood private plane" in notes — sorry for the voice-to-text.
[01:40] Luis (SRE): On network side, we need details for the VPC peering and the IP ranges the gateway will use. Also curious about egress rules if we failover to a hosted fallback — is that a hard egress to Redwood region or can it be kept inside our VPC?
[01:58] Marta (CSM): Quick interjection — Avery and Ravi can provide the VPC connection matrix and the fallback behavior options. We'll mark the fallback as configurable: you can allow host fallback or keep everything private with no fallback.
[02:15] Anya (PM): For success criteria, we're looking at sub-200ms median token latency and p95 below 500ms for the standard chat flow. If we can't reach that on dedicated, we need clear cost tradeoffs and quantization options.
[02:35] Ravi (SE): That aligns. The bench you ran shows medians ~150ms when batching is applied, but p99 goes to ~1.1s on cold paths. Two levers: add more capacity (Dedicated) or enable longer prefix caching to reduce KV populates. There's also quantized model variants that save cost but might shift quality.
[02:55] Dana (CTO): We have a hard requirement on accuracy for our clinical triage prompts, so quality drop is a non-starter unless we validate on held-out prompt sets.
[03:12] Avery (AE): Understood. We'll recommend running the Redwood Optimize evals against your prompt set to quantify any regressions. We can run a controlled A/B and get you metrics.
[03:28] Priya (Security): Back to SAML — our IdP is Okta. We need a sample SAML metadata file and a step-by-step to map groups to RBAC roles. Also SSO session timeout defaults.
[03:45] Ravi (SE): We'll send the Okta quickstart + an example mapping. Small warning — sometimes the assertion consumer URL needs the exact gateway host, and transcripts or guides may show a placeholder that confuses teams. We'll include the live example you should paste.
[04:03] Jamal (Platform): On the bench we ran a 50-concurrent synthetic load with 8 token avg reply — results are in the sheet. However, one run had an outlier where latency doubled; that was the cold start and we didn't pre-warm the KV cache. How do you recommend pre-warm?
[04:22] Ravi (SE): Two patterns: run a warmed prefix sweep or use automated prefix caching via the SDK. For your case, a warm sweep of the common prefixes and enabling continuous batching with a 20ms max delay helped us.
[04:40] Luis (SRE): Any firewall ports? We want the minimal egress set.
[04:47] Avery (AE): We'll attach the VPC firewall matrix. Typically HTTPS to the gateway endpoint and the control plane port for the private deployment — exact ports differ by deployment mode; we'll include both hosted and private specifics.
[05:05] Priya (Security): Also please list what logs are available for audit (token-level traces, prompt redaction options), and the retention options. We need to ensure PII redaction paths exist.
[05:22] Marta (CSM): We expose per-route telemetry and you can opt-out of storing full prompts; Redwood gives structured metadata and hashed prompt IDs if you choose. We'll share the docs on retention and redaction.
[05:40] Anya (PM): Regarding timelines, we need staging gate cleared by next Friday to hit internal demo on the 30th. Is that feasible?
[05:52] Avery (AE): Feasible if we get SAML creds and KMS contact this week and you run the micro-benchmarks with the warm pattern. Action items we agreed to capture after the call.
[06:07] Jamal (Platform): One more — what happens if Dedicated capacity is saturated? Do we overflow to a cheaper variant or block?
[06:18] Ravi (SE): We can configure smart routing: overflow to compatible model variants (e.g., smaller quantized variant) or fall back to hosted tier. We recommend a canary policy: route 95% to primary, 5% to fallback to validate the degraded path.
[06:35] Priya (Security): Any compliance paperwork like SOC 2 or ISO we can get quickly? We need the attestation for procurement.
[06:43] Marta (CSM): We'll upload the SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary to the shared folder. Expect a link within one business day.
[06:55] Dana (CTO): Ok good. So to be explicit, our immediate blockers are: SAML metadata import, KMS contact + rotation confirmation, and an agreed bench run pattern for warm-up.
[07:10] Avery (AE): Noted. We'll send materials and schedule the bench replay session. Any other final items?
[07:18] Luis (SRE): Please include a short checklist of what to verify post-VPC peering to ensure the gateway is reachable from our subnets.
[07:26] Avery (AE): Will do.
[07:30] Marta (CSM): Recap of next steps now and then I'll drop in the shared doc with owners.

Recap / Next Steps (verbatim):
- Redwood: Share SAML/Okta quickstart + example assertion consumer URL and RBAC mapping. (Owner: Avery)
- Redwood: Share KMS integration doc and HSM guidelines; confirm rotation hooks. (Owner: Ravi)
- Customer: Run benchmark with warm prefix pattern and upload CSV to shared drive. (Owner: Jamal)
- Customer: Confirm KMS admin contact and rotation window. (Owner: Priya)
- Redwood: Upload SOC 2 + ISO docs to folder. (Owner: Marta)

End of transcript.
